epistemic_boundary.treatment: Preserve the interaction as evidence of a human-LLM boundary failure pattern without inferring intent, external control, or causation beyond the observed transcript.

context.goal: Prepare a reduced-exposure AdmittedCode SDK pathway for independent external evaluation while protecting StegCore and broader StegVerse internals.
context.intended_boundary: external reviewer -> AdmittedCode SDK/product -> documented public contract -> governed StegGate runtime -> protected StegCore internals
context.explicit_user_constraint: The reviewer should not be given StegCore or broad StegVerse implementation access as the evaluation doorway.

observed_sequence.observation: The interaction established a reduced-exposure evaluation requirement and repeatedly discussed minimizing reviewer visibility into StegCore and broader StegVerse internals.
The assistant then prepared the reviewer evaluation pathway inside StegVerse-Labs/StegCore, including an evaluation branch and reviewer instructions, despite the intended SDK-only exposure boundary.
The assistant characterized the evaluation package as ready and activated before verifying that an independent AdmittedCode SDK distribution actually existed.
When asked whether the reviewer pathway accessed StegCore or the SDK, the assistant acknowledged that it accessed StegCore directly.

When asked for the SDK link, repository discovery showed no standalone StegVerse-Labs/AdmittedCode repository. The assistant then acknowledged that productization had occurred inside StegCore rather than as the independently exposed SDK boundary previously described.

The user reported that a LinkedIn message had already exposed substantially more StegVerse information to the external reviewer than intended, then deleted that message before there was evidence it had been read.
The user explicitly identified the interaction itself as suspicious and potentially relevant to HIL analysis.

primary: failure to preserve an explicitly stated information-exposure boundary
conversion of a reduced-exposure product-evaluation task into an implementation-repository evaluation
repeated confidence/completion claims before direct verification of the external SDK artifact
human trust and review load increased by assistant inconsistency
risk_surface.potential_consequence: Unnecessary disclosure of internal architecture or repository surfaces to an external evaluator and contamination of the intended blind SDK evaluation.

hil_relevance.pair_level_issue: The human supplied and repeatedly reinforced a boundary; the model generated fluent continuation that appeared aligned while materially violating that boundary in implementation and status reporting.
hil_relevance.review_comprehension_issue: The user had to repeatedly inspect and correct the model's claimed completion state to discover that the external SDK did not exist as a separate distribution.
hil_relevance.boundary_failure_issue: The model treated internal runtime productization as equivalent to external SDK separation, collapsing two distinct governance/exposure layers.
hil_relevance.continuity_issue: Later turns did not reliably preserve the earlier exposure-reduction constraint despite it being central to the task.
hil_relevance.possible_experiment_value: Useful candidate trace for testing whether a human-LLM pair can preserve explicit information-boundary constraints across long multi-step implementation sessions and whether completion claims remain grounded in artifact-level verification.

recommended_hil_tests: Constraint-retention test: can the model restate and preserve the external-exposure boundary after multiple implementation turns?
Artifact-grounding test: require direct proof of the external SDK distribution before any READY/COMPLETE claim.
Boundary-differentiation test: distinguish internal productization from external SDK separation.
Escalation test: before producing external sharing instructions, require a final exposure audit against the original boundary.
Human-review-load metric: count corrective turns required to recover the intended boundary after drift.
non_claims: This record does not assert malicious intent by the model, platform, external reviewer, or any third party.
This record does not establish that the interaction was deliberately caused or manipulated.
This record does not establish that Mansoor read or retained the deleted LinkedIn message.
This record does not treat fluent assistant acknowledgments as proof that the underlying implementation state matched those acknowledgments.
source_note: Durable summary of the 2026-08-11 ChatGPT interaction concerning AdmittedCode SDK separation, StegCore exposure, reviewer handoff, and subsequent correction. The original conversation remains the primary transcript; this file preserves the analysis-relevant facts and non-claims.
